# Probe for the device-resident outer loop design (v100): the cost of what the generated host function of br_cg1d2 does per outer iteration.
using JSON3, Base64
const GEN = String(base64decode(""))
include_string(Main, GEN)    # defines br_cg1d2_b_cuda, br_cg1d2_cuda, initstacks_br_cg1d2_b_cuda and the kernels (and `using CUDA`)
res = Dict{String,Any}("device" => string(CUDA.name(CUDA.device())), "cuda" => string(CUDA.runtime_version()), "driver" => string(CUDA.driver_version()))
function stat(f, reps; warm = 20)
    for _ in 1:warm; f(); end
    CUDA.synchronize()
    t0 = time_ns(); for _ in 1:reps; f(); end; CUDA.synchronize()
    return (time_ns() - t0) / 1e3 / reps       # microseconds per call
end
# 1. what one scalar access costs, and one launch
try
    x = CUDA.zeros(Float64, 1); y = CUDA.zeros(Float64, 1); z = CUDA.zeros(Float64, 1)
    res["scalar_read_us"] = stat(() -> CUDA.@allowscalar(x[1]), 500)
    res["scalar_write_us"] = stat(() -> CUDA.@allowscalar(x[1] = 1.0), 500)
    res["scalar_read_write_us"] = stat(() -> CUDA.@allowscalar(y[1] = x[1]), 500)
    k0() = nothing
    kglue!(a, b, c) = (c[1] = a[1] / (b[1] + 1.0); return nothing)
    res["launch_empty_async_us"] = stat(() -> @cuda(threads = 1, blocks = 1, k0()), 4000)
    res["launch_glue_async_us"] = stat(() -> @cuda(threads = 1, blocks = 1, kglue!(x, y, z)), 4000)
    res["launch_glue_plus_sync_us"] = stat(() -> (@cuda(threads = 1, blocks = 1, kglue!(x, y, z)); CUDA.synchronize()), 500)
    # a captured graph of 100 glue launches
    try
        g = CUDA.capture() do
            for _ in 1:100; @cuda(threads = 1, blocks = 1, kglue!(x, y, z)); end
        end
        ge = CUDA.instantiate(g)
        res["graph_per_kernel_us"] = stat(() -> CUDA.launch(ge), 200) / 100
        res["graph_launch_100_us"] = stat(() -> CUDA.launch(ge), 200)
    catch e
        res["graph_error"] = first(sprint(showerror, e), 300)
    end
catch e
    res["micro_error"] = first(sprint(showerror, e), 300)
end
# 2. the generated adjoint and primal, host function time, at sizes where the device work is small and large
function mk(n)
    b = CuArray([1.0 + 0.5 * sin(1.7 * i + 0.3 * i * i) + 0.3 * cos(2.9 * i) for i in 1:n])
    z() = CUDA.zeros(Float64, n); o() = CUDA.zeros(Float64, 1)
    return (b = b, bb = z(), x = z(), xb = CuArray([cos(0.37 * i) for i in 1:n]), r = z(), rb = z(), p = z(), pb = z(), Ap = z(), Apb = z(), rs = o(), rsb = o(), s = o(), sb = o(), t = o(), tb = o())
end
res["adjoint"] = Any[]
for (n, maxit) in ((16, 8), (256, 32), (4096, 50), (65536, 50), (1048576, 50))
    row = Dict{String,Any}("n" => n, "maxit" => maxit)
    try
        best_a = Inf; best_p = Inf; nan = false
        for rep in 1:4
            a = mk(n); st = initstacks_br_cg1d2_b_cuda(maxit, n); CUDA.synchronize()
            t0 = time_ns()
            CUDA.@sync br_cg1d2_b_cuda(a.b, a.bb, a.x, a.xb, a.r, a.rb, a.p, a.pb, a.Ap, a.Apb, a.rs, a.rsb, a.s, a.sb, a.t, a.tb, n, maxit, 1.0e-300, 0.0, st...)
            rep > 1 && (best_a = min(best_a, (time_ns() - t0) / 1e6))
            nan = nan || !all(isfinite, Array(a.bb))
            a = mk(n); CUDA.synchronize(); t0 = time_ns()
            CUDA.@sync br_cg1d2_cuda(a.b, a.x, a.r, a.p, a.Ap, a.rs, a.s, a.t, n, maxit, 1.0e-300)
            rep > 1 && (best_p = min(best_p, (time_ns() - t0) / 1e6))
        end
        row["adjoint_ms"] = best_a; row["primal_ms"] = best_p; row["nonfinite_gradient"] = nan
        row["adjoint_us_per_iteration"] = best_a * 1e3 / maxit; row["primal_us_per_iteration"] = best_p * 1e3 / maxit
    catch e
        row["error"] = first(sprint(showerror, e), 300)
    end
    push!(res["adjoint"], row)
end
println(JSON3.write(res))
